title: WDBX V2: Observable Memory, Multimodal Inputs, and Research Alignment
body: The second iteration of the WDBX runtime ships an observable pipeline: block-chain memory with temporal queries, multimodal input fusion, an async neural job queue, and a research-alignment telemetry layer that scores every turn against the constitution.

title: On Saying “I'm Not Sure”
body: A note in Abbey's voice — the empathetic-polymath persona — on why an honest “I don't know” is one of the most useful things an agent can say.

title: Inside the WDBX Hybrid Ranker: Four Factors, One Score
body: Semantic similarity is only the first of four factors. Here is the exact score WDBX uses to rank retrieval candidates — and why every factor is bounded to [0,1].

title: How Sparse Evidence Attention Decides What the Model Sees
body: Before a model reasons, something must choose which records reach the context window. SEA scores eight criteria, then packs greedily under a hard token budget.

title: The Weights Behind Abbey, Aviva, and Abi
body: Persona routing is not a hidden model call. It is a normalized weight vector with hard policy overrides and an inspectable strategy decision.

title: Designing AI Systems That Can Explain Their Last Move
body: A practical guide to capturing retrieval paths, policy checks, and operator decisions so teams can debug autonomous workflows after the fact.

title: What We Measure Before Calling an Agent Production-Ready
body: Latency and accuracy are not enough. We track tool-boundary violations, source coverage, rollback paths, abstention quality, and human-review burden.

title: From Vector Search to Weighted Backtrace Graphs
body: Why retrieval infrastructure needs relationship-aware context and why ranking alone is not sufficient for high-stakes answer generation.

title: The Case for Separate Planning, Review, and Execution Agents
body: Role separation lets teams encode checks and balances into an AI workflow instead of relying on a single agent to police itself.

title: Making AI Control Surfaces Feel Calm Under Pressure
body: Interface details that prevent overload: progressive disclosure, confidence bands, decision diffs, and emergency stop affordances.

title: What Incident Reviews Need From AI Logs
body: How to structure traces so teams can reconstruct context, model output, policy decisions, tool calls, and human overrides after a production event.

title: Private AI Does Not Mean Invisible AI
body: Offline and VPC deployments still need measurable controls: local audit trails, release gates, repeatable evals, and operator-visible confidence signals.

title: Neural Backtracking: What a Block Chain Buys an AI Memory
body: Hallucination debugging is archaeology. WDBX chains every interaction block to its parent so you can walk back to the exact moment a model drifted — and prove nobody edited the record.

title: Surviving Writergate: Migrating ABI to Zig 0.16
body: Zig 0.16 rebuilt std.io around vtable-based Reader and Writer interfaces. Ninety-five files later, here's what the migration actually looked like — and the patterns we standardized on.

title: Why WDBX Is Written in Zig
body: Garbage collection pauses are invisible in the mean and fatal in the tail. WDBX is Zig because a real-time vector database is a p99 product, not a p50 product.

title: A six-layer architecture for evidence-aware AI systems
body: Quesar organizes interface, orchestration, retrieval, acceleration, storage, and audit as distinct layers so that evidence and runtime claims can be traced to the component that actually supports them.

title: A private document pipeline with explicit fallback behavior
body: The private Quesar application implements bounded ingestion, workspace-scoped extraction and search, and consent-gated model access while making degraded retrieval behavior visible instead of silently changing providers.

title: Mobile Vault persistence across CloudKit and local fallback
body: The Quesar mobile Vault keeps one CRUD contract while selecting either the user's private CloudKit database or an encrypted local SecureStore fallback and exposing the selected backend to the application.

title: Quasar as a bounded repository-generation loop
body: Quasar couples an Anthropic tool loop to a narrowly constrained project filesystem, producing a local application through inspectable read, list, and write operations rather than granting an unconstrained shell.

title: Abbey capability claims as an executable ledger
body: Abbey centralizes capability statements in a typed registry whose status, evidence, dependencies, feature flags, and refusal behavior can be projected into documentation and checked for drift.

title: WDBX Specimen separates architecture, runtime profiles, and proof
body: WDBX Specimen combines a provenance-aware architecture specification with explicit browser and native runtime profiles, then uses conformance tests to make a bounded subset of the design executable.

title: Deterministic research exports with citation gates
body: The Quesar research export pipeline converts validated publication records into stable JSON and static HTML, verifies and copies declared attachments, and records content digests while enforcing unique identifiers, public source URLs, and canonical links.
